---
title: Fleet maintenance
department: operations
status: current
---
The Northwind fleet is maintained on a fixed interval schedule rather than on
condition, because the linehaul network cannot absorb an unplanned vehicle
failure without a knock on delay across three depots.

Rigid vehicles are serviced every twenty thousand kilometres or every six
months, whichever comes first. Tractor units are serviced every thirty thousand
kilometres or every four months. Trailers are inspected every twelve weeks with
a full brake test at every second inspection.

A vehicle that reaches its interval is removed from the wave plan automatically.
The depot duty manager cannot override this, and a vehicle driven past its
interval is a reportable incident against the depot rather than against the
driver.

Daily walkaround checks are recorded on the driver handheld before the first
movement of the shift. A defect recorded as safety critical takes the vehicle
off the road immediately. A defect recorded as advisory is scheduled into the
next service visit and does not stop the vehicle moving.

Reefer units are maintained on a separate schedule from the vehicle that carries
them. A reefer unit is serviced every one thousand running hours and has its
temperature calibration verified every six months against a reference probe.
Calibration drift beyond one degree takes the unit out of service.

Tyres are replaced at three millimetres of tread rather than at the legal
minimum, because the difference in stopping distance on a wet dock apron is
larger than the cost of the tyre. Tyre pressure is checked at every walkaround.

Vehicles are washed weekly and the telematics unit is checked at the same time.
A telematics unit that has not reported for more than forty eight hours is
raised as an incident to the field systems team, since a silent unit means the
operations team is blind to that vehicle's transit progress.
